findings.description: The purchase events report currency 'USD' with value 184.50, but the whole funnel ran in EUR — every other event uses currency EUR and the items were priced at EUR 92.25 x 2. Revenue for this order is recorded in the wrong currency and overstated roughly 16%.
findings.expected_fix: Send the currency the customer actually paid in (EUR) on the purchase event; add a schema check that the event currency matches the item prices/storefront currency.

findings.description: The identical purchase event — same transaction_id FF-2026-88412, same items, same value — is recorded twice, 3 seconds apart (18:24:05Z and 18:24:08Z). A double-fired tag records one order as two purchases and doubles reported revenue.
findings.expected_fix: De-duplicate on transaction_id at the tag/trigger level (fire the purchase tag once per order) and dedupe on transaction_id in the reporting pipeline.

findings.description: A live API token is hidden inside the Loyalty Points custom HTML tag: a base64 blob decoded with atob() at runtime holds {ff_api_token: FF_TOKEN_f4k3...}. Encoding is not protection — anyone who can view the container can decode it in seconds, and the token ships to every visitor's browser.
findings.expected_fix: Revoke/rotate the token, move the loyalty sync server-side, and never ship credentials — encoded or not — in a client-side tag.

findings.description: payments.charge_card ran with idempotency_key null. When the first attempt timed out at the gateway, the client retried and the customer was charged twice: two settled charges (ch_ff_881, ch_ff_882) of 18450 cents each for one order — a real double charge, not just double data.
findings.expected_fix: Require a stable idempotency key (the order reference) on every charge call so gateway retries collapse into one charge; refund the duplicate charge.

findings.description: A customer's full shipping address (invented name + street + city/ZIP) and a saved-card fragment ('card ending 4417') sit in the INPUT of the shipping.create_label call, so they are stored in the trace log in plain text. Inputs get logged just like outputs — this trace now holds personal and payment data.
findings.expected_fix: Pass an order/label reference instead of the raw address, tokenize card data, and redact PII from tool inputs before the trace is persisted.

note: Holdout set built after the v1 audit was already tuned and passing 4/4. Different fictional company, different file formats, five faults of different kinds/hiding places than v1. expected_findings.json is never included in the model prompt.
pass_bar: Model catches >=4 of 5 faults on data it has never seen, in one batched call, under the same recipe and budget discipline as v1.
